subject: Startups
title: The Founder's Dilemma: Passion vs. Market
description: Learn The Founder's Dilemma: Passion vs. Market in one minute.

hook.text: Founders love their original idea. Markets don't care about your feelings—they care about their problems.

buildup.text: Many founders resist pivoting because the new direction doesn't match their personal vision or passion.

discovery.text: The best founders detach their ego from the product. They fall in love with the problem, not their solution.

twist.text: Stewart Butterfield loved games but built Slack. His passion shifted when he saw a bigger opportunity.

climax.text: Passion for the user's problem beats passion for your idea. That mindset makes pivots feel natural, not painful.

punchline.text: Love the problem, not your first solution to it.

quiz.question: What should founders fall in love with, according to pivot wisdom?
